# LAND-001 — feature contract (frozen for execution run 1)

**Status:** frozen. Implementers do not edit this file; see `docs/shared-contract.md` §4
for the amendment protocol.
**Machine-checkable half:** [`apps/web/src/api/auth.types.ts`](../../../apps/web/src/api/auth.types.ts)
(API shapes) and [`apps/web/src/features/landing/types.ts`](../../../apps/web/src/features/landing/types.ts)
(shell ↔ landing seam). Where this prose and those types disagree, the types win.

---

## 0. Scope decision for this run

Decision taken by the instructor with the repo owner (2026-09-06):

> **Full SRS-AUTH-001 shapes on the frontend; every server-dependent control is wired to
> a hardcoded mock client.** No backend is built in this run.

Concretely:

- The SPA is written against the *real* endpoint shapes in SRS-AUTH-001 §3.7 — request
  bodies, status codes, error envelope, cookie semantics — so that swapping the mock for
  the generated client later changes **one file** (`apps/web/src/api/auth.ts`) and no
  component.
- `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts` exports `authApi: AuthApi`. In this run its implementation is
  an in-memory mock (§3). It is the **only** place that knows the server doesn't exist.
- Components never branch on "mock vs real". They call `authApi` and handle `ApiFailure`.

This deliberately runs ahead of roadmap Phase 1 on *shape* but not on *infrastructure*:
no Go, no Postgres, no Redis, no Google OAuth app registration are introduced.

### Story conflicts resolved here

1. **Registration → dashboard vs. enumeration protection.** `acceptance-criteria.md` says a
   new registrant lands on the dashboard, and also that a duplicate registration produces
   "the same neutral next step a successful registration would produce." Both cannot hold
   if success sets a session. SRS FR-08 (priority M) wins: **`POST /register` never sets a
   session and always returns the same 202 body.** The modal shows
   `landing.auth.signup_next_step`; the visitor then logs in via the Log in tab (FR-03
   permits login before verification). TC-06's "redirected to dashboard" is therefore
   satisfied *via login*, not directly — recorded as a story amendment for integration.
2. **Session probe endpoint.** SRS §3.7 has no "who am I" endpoint, and the SPA cannot read
   httpOnly cookies. This contract adds **`GET /api/v1/users/me`** (user-service; a shared
   endpoint per `frontend.md` §6) as the session probe. Flagged for the SRS/user-service
   spec at integration.
3. **Google OAuth without a server.** The authorize URL is a real server route in the SRS.
   In mock mode `authApi.googleAuthorizeUrl()` returns the SPA route
   **`/__mock/oauth/google`**, where the shell renders a stand-in consent page with
   Approve / Deny (§3.4). The landing page does `window.location.assign(url)` either way,
   exactly as it will against the real redirect.
4. **Amendment 1 (integration, 2026-09-06) — CSRF token after reload.** FR-12 keeps the
   CSRF token in SPA memory only. After a page reload the boot probe restores the session
   but the SPA holds no token, so it cannot make *any* state-changing call — observed as
   Log out silently doing nothing. Resolution (additive): `GET /users/me` returns
   `{ user, csrf_token }`, re-issuing the session-bound token. `AuthApi.me()` now resolves
   `SessionInfo | null`. Both slices had finished; both were re-verified against the amended
   shape (shell: `AuthContext` stores the probe's token and always attempts
   `authApi.logout`; landing: unaffected — it never calls `me()`). Flag for the SRS
   alongside §0.2.
5. **Licensed media, run 2 (2026-09-06).** The visual redesign ported from `template/`
   carries three third-party media items into the shipping app (see `docs/design-system.md`
   §5): `public/media/saitama-vs-garou.mp4` (hero backdrop, `Hero.tsx`),
   `public/media/download.jpg` (Pricing side art, `Pricing.tsx`), and a live Pinterest pin
   embed (`Quote.tsx`).

## 1. HTTP surface the SPA is written against

Base path `/api/v1`. Every error uses the envelope
`{ "error": { "code": "<ErrorCode>", "message": "<server-localized>" } }`. Codes are the
generated `ErrorCode` union in `apps/web/src/api/generated/audit.ts` — no others exist.
Every request carries `Accept-Language: <i18n.resolvedLanguage>`. State-changing
requests carry `X-CSRF-Token` (FR-24). Cookies are httpOnly and never read by the SPA.

| Endpoint | Method | Request | Success | Errors (status → code) | SRS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/auth/register` | POST | `{ email, password }` | **202** `{ "status": "pending_verification" }` — identical whether or not the email exists; **no cookies set** | 400 → `VALIDATION_FAILED`; 429 → `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` | FR-01, FR-02, FR-04, FR-08 |
| `/auth/login` | POST | `{ email, password }` | **200** `{ "csrf_token": string }` + access & refresh cookies | 401 → `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (unknown email *and* bad password — identical); 403 → `AUTH_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`; 429 → `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After: <seconds>`; 400 → `VALIDATION_FAILED` | FR-10, FR-12, FR-13, FR-14 |
| `/auth/logout` | POST (CSRF) | — | **204**, cookies cleared | 401 → `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`; 403 → `AUTH_CSRF_FAILED` | FR-32 |
| `/auth/oauth/google` | GET (browser navigation) | — | 302 → Google consent | — | FR-05, SEC-05 |
| `/auth/oauth/google/callback` | GET (browser) | — | Sets cookies, **302 → `/dashboard`**. On denial/cancel: **302 → `/?auth_error=oauth_cancelled`**, no cookies | — | FR-05 |
| `/users/me` | GET | — | **200** `{ user: { id, email, role, tier }, csrf_token }` | 401 → `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` / `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` | (added, §0.2; amended, §0.4) |

**Validation the client performs before any request (AC "client-side validation"):**
email must match a basic `local@domain.tld` shape; password length ≥ **10** (FR-02, no
composition rules). Submit stays disabled until both pass; no request is sent otherwise.

**Rate-limit behaviour the client honours:** on `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, disable submit for
`retryAfterSeconds` (from `Retry-After`, default 30 if absent) and show
`landing.auth.error_rate_limited`. A visible countdown, if shown, is a number and goes
through `formatNumber`.

**Network failure:** any transport failure / timeout surfaces as `ApiFailure{kind:"network"}`;
the modal ends the loading state, shows `landing.auth.error_unreachable`, keeps the email.

## 2. TypeScript contract — `apps/web/src/api/auth.types.ts`

Authoritative; reproduced here for readers without the repo open.

```ts
export interface RegisterRequest { email: string; password: string }
export interface RegisterResponse { status: "pending_verification" }
export interface LoginRequest { email: string; password: string }
export interface LoginResponse { csrf_token: string }
export interface CurrentUser { id: string; email: string; role: Role; tier: string }
export interface SessionInfo { user: CurrentUser; csrf_token: string }   // amendment 1

export type ApiFailure =
  | { kind: "http"; status: number; error: ApiError; retryAfterSeconds?: number }
  | { kind: "network" };
export class ApiRequestError extends Error { readonly failure: ApiFailure }

export interface AuthApi {
  register(req: RegisterRequest, opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<RegisterResponse>;
  login(req: LoginRequest, opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<LoginResponse>;
  logout(csrfToken: string, opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<void>;
  /** Session probe. Resolves null on 401 rather than throwing. */
  me(opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<SessionInfo | null>;
  /** URL to navigate the browser to. Never fetched. */
  googleAuthorizeUrl(): string;
}
```

`apps/web/src/api/auth.ts` exports `export const authApi: AuthApi`. Everything else in the
app imports **only** `authApi` and the types.

## 3. Mock client behaviour (`apps/web/src/api/auth.ts`, this run)

Owned by slice `LAND-001-fe-shell`. Must be deterministic enough for the test cases.

- **Seed accounts:** `returning@example.com` / `Str0ng-Passw0rd!` and `taken@example.com`
  / `Str0ng-Passw0rd!`. Store is in-memory, initialised from `sessionStorage` key
  `gs.mock.users` so a registration survives a reload within the tab.
- **Session:** `sessionStorage` key `gs.mock.session` = `{ userId, csrfToken }`. `me()`
  reads it. `login` writes it; `logout` clears it. (Stands in for the httpOnly cookie jar.)
- **Latency:** every call resolves/rejects after ~400–700 ms so loading states are visible.
- **register:** validation failure → 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Otherwise 202
  `{status:"pending_verification"}` whether or not the email exists; creates the account
  only if new. Never sets a session.
- **login:** unknown email or wrong password → 401 `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, identical
  timing. **5 consecutive failures for one email** → subsequent attempts return 429
  `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` with `retryAfterSeconds: 30` until 30 s have passed (FR-13); success
  resets the counter.
- **Offline simulation:** if `sessionStorage.getItem("gs.mock.offline") === "1"` **or** the
  page URL has `?mock=offline`, every call rejects with `{kind:"network"}` (TC-19).
- **googleAuthorizeUrl():** returns `/__mock/oauth/google`.
- **Mock consent page** (shell route `/__mock/oauth/google`): Approve → sets a session for a
  Google-created user `google.user@example.com` (creating it if absent, role `user`) and
  navigates to `/dashboard`; Deny → navigates to `/?auth_error=oauth_cancelled`.
- Switch: `VITE_AUTH_MOCK` — `"true"` (default when unset) uses the mock. Any other value
  is reserved for the future generated client and may simply throw "not implemented"; do
  not build a real HTTP client in this run.

## 4. Shell ↔ landing seam — `apps/web/src/features/landing/types.ts`

The landing slice may import from `styles/`, `i18n/`, `api/`, and its own subtree
**only** — never `app/`, never the router. The shell imports the slice.

```ts
export type LandingNotice = "oauth_cancelled";

export interface LandingPageProps {
  /** Called after a successful email/password login. Shell stores the CSRF token,
   *  marks the session live and navigates to /dashboard. */
  onAuthenticated: (session: { csrfToken: string }) => void;
  /** Non-blocking notice to show on mount (from ?auth_error=...). */
  notice?: LandingNotice | null;
  /** Called when the visitor dismisses the notice; shell clears the query param. */
  onNoticeDismiss?: () => void;
}
```

`apps/web/src/features/landing/index.ts` exports `LandingPage: (props: LandingPageProps) => JSX.Element`.

Routing responsibilities (shell): `/` → if session live, `<Navigate to="/dashboard" replace>`
**before** rendering the landing page; else `<LandingPage …>`. `/dashboard` → protected
placeholder (redirects to `/` when no session). `/__mock/oauth/google` → mock consent.
Session state comes from one boot-time `authApi.me()` probe; while it is pending the
shell renders `common.loading`, never the landing page (AC: no flash of marketing for an
authenticated visitor).

Anchor navigation inside the landing page uses plain `<a href="#features">` etc.; the
section ids are **`features`, `how-it-works`, `pricing`** and the main landmark id is
**`main`** (skip link target).

## 5. i18n

All `landing.*` keys already exist in both catalogs. The shell's keys are pre-seeded
under `app.*`. **Only slice `LAND-001-fe-landing` may add keys**, under `landing.*`, to both
catalogs in the same change. Voice-critical keys (`landing.hero.*`) are already listed in
`apps/web/src/i18n/voice-critical-keys.json` — do not alter their wording.

Parity check (Python is not installed on the owner's machine; this is equivalent for the
frontend set):

```bash
node -e "const a=require('./apps/web/src/i18n/locales/en-US.json'),b=require('./apps/web/src/i18n/locales/vi-VN.json');const f=(o,p='')=>Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k,v])=>typeof v==='object'?f(v,p+k+'.'):[p+k]);const A=new Set(f(a)),B=new Set(f(b));const m=[...A].filter(k=>!B.has(k)),x=[...B].filter(k=>!A.has(k));if(m.length||x.length){console.error({missing_in_vi:m,extra_in_vi:x});process.exit(1)}console.log('i18n parity ok',A.size)"
```

## 6. Error-code → SPA string policy

Default: render the SPA's own key via `errorMessageKey()` from `i18n/errorMessages.ts`.
`renderServerMessage()` is **not** permitted anywhere in LAND-001 — no story clause allows
it. Unknown codes fall back per `frontend.md` §6.
